sections.title: Form and life history
sections.text: Miersiella umbellata is a tiny rhizomatous herb of South American tropical forests. Lacking chlorophyll, it is mycoheterotrophic: it depends on soil fungi for resources and does not photosynthesise.

sections.title: Stem and flowers
sections.text: The pale stem bears scales and a terminal umbel of 4–10 flowers, sometimes more. Each flower is about 2.5–4.5 mm long. The rhizome bears roots and scales; the fruit is a capsule.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No reliable food use is known for this inconspicuous plant.
